name: Wagga Wagga Botanic Gardens
description: The Wagga Wagga Botanic Gardens sit at the base of Willans Hill and cover 22 acres. Within the grounds are a mini zoo, a free flight aviary, a children's adventure playground and a rainforest section, plus the Tree Chapel and a Chinese Pavilion. Garden areas showcase camellias, cacti and succulents, proteas, Australian natives and roses. Covered barbecues are available and the Willans Hill Miniature Railway runs through the gardens on the first and third Sunday of each month.
highlights: Mini zoo and free flight aviary
Children's adventure playground
Tree Chapel and Chinese Pavilion
Camellia, cactus, protea, native and rose gardens
Covered barbecues and picnic areas

name: Museum of the Riverina - Botanic Gardens Site
description: The Botanic Gardens site is one of the Museum of the Riverina's two venues, sitting beside the Wagga Wagga Botanic Gardens. It runs changing exhibitions along with workshops, events and school programs, and includes a historic schoolhouse in its grounds. General admission is free and all public spaces are wheelchair accessible by lift and pathway.
highlights: Free general admission
Changing exhibitions, workshops and events
Historic schoolhouse on site
Accessible parking bay near the entrance
Free tea, coffee and water in the Community Education Space

name: Museum of the Riverina - Historic Council Chambers
description: The Historic Council Chambers on Baylis Street is the Museum of the Riverina's city-centre site. The museum is a social history museum combining touring shows of national significance with local stories, and across its two sites it cares for more than 15,000 objects, photographs, textiles and paper-based materials.
highlights: City-centre site in the historic council chambers
Touring exhibitions of national significance
Collection of more than 15,000 objects
Wheelchair accessible

name: Wagga Wagga Art Gallery
addressLine: Morrow Street, Civic Centre corner Baylis Street
description: Wagga Wagga Art Gallery shows work by Riverina artists alongside touring exhibitions from around Australia, with about forty exhibitions and displays each year. Its showpiece is the National Art Glass Gallery, home to Australia's largest and most significant collection of contemporary art glass, holding roughly 400 pieces.
highlights: National Art Glass Gallery and the National Art Glass Collection
Around 40 exhibitions and displays a year
Gallery shop
Wheelchair accessible with support for vision and hearing loss

name: Willans Hill Miniature Railway
description: The Willans Hill Miniature Railway runs inside the Wagga Wagga Botanic Gardens, with an authentic station and booking office. The track weaves through a garden setting, woodlands, a tunnel and over a bridge. Trains run on the first and third Sunday of each month, and covered footwear is essential to ride. An invitation run each November brings model train enthusiasts from around Australia.
highlights: Runs the first and third Sunday of each month
Track through woodlands, a tunnel and over a bridge
Authentic station and booking office
Annual invitation run each November
Covered footwear required to ride

name: Wagga Wagga Rail Heritage Station Museum
description: Set on the platform of the historic Wagga Wagga Railway Station, this museum displays photographs and railway memorabilia covering the local history of the railway. Across the railway pedestrian bridge are the Rail Heritage Gang Sheds, holding railway trikes, tools and photographs in two sheds once used by track maintenance gangs, and a model trains display with several working HO and N scale layouts. The three locations keep different opening times.
highlights: On the historic Wagga Wagga Railway Station platform
Gang Sheds display of railway trikes and tools
Working HO and N scale model railway layouts
Three separate display locations

name: Wagga Steam and Vintage Engine Museum
addressLine: Lord Baden Powell Drive, Willans Hill
description: Operated by the Wagga Historic Engine Club Inc, this museum displays working engines including shearing machines and all types of stationary engines, along with vintage steam and oil engines. It opens on the first and third Sunday of the month, or by appointment, for a gold coin donation.
highlights: Run by the Wagga Historic Engine Club Inc
Working steam, oil and stationary engines
Shearing machinery on display
Open first and third Sunday of the month, or by appointment
Gold coin donation entry

name: RAAF Wagga Aviation Heritage Centre
description: The RAAF Wagga Aviation Heritage Centre covers Air Force history and the RAAF's involvement in the Riverina. Static display aircraft beside the centre represent more than 50 years of RAAF flying history and can be viewed and photographed up close. Inside, heritage artefacts are set out in themed rooms including a Community Room with a rotating display on military history and the contribution of people from Wagga Wagga and the Riverina.
highlights: Static display aircraft spanning over 50 years of RAAF flying
Themed display rooms of Air Force artefacts
Community Room with rotating regional displays
Last remaining Riverina World War II base of its network
Car park and public toilets

name: Lake Albert
description: Lake Albert is one of Wagga's most used recreational areas, catering for boating, fishing, swimming and other aquatic activities. A five-and-a-half kilometre circuit walking track rings the lake and is popular with walkers, joggers and bike riders, with eight fitness stations set over 800 metres on the eastern side. Boat ramps are at Bosley Park next to the Wagga Wagga Boat Club and at Apex Park, which also has a children's playground with a separate fenced area for smaller children.
highlights: 5.5 km circuit walking and cycling track
Eight outdoor fitness stations on the eastern side
Boat ramps at Bosley Park and Apex Park
Playground with fenced area for small children
Dog friendly on leads

name: Riverside Wagga Beach
description: Riverside Wagga Beach is a sandy river beach on the Murrumbidgee about five minutes from the CBD, with grassed shady picnic areas, sheltered barbecues, sculptures and event spaces. Swimmers cool off in the river during the warmer months and paddlers launch kayaks and canoes from here. It also has a large destination playground catering for all ages and abilities, food and drink vans nearby, and forms part of the Wiradjuri Walking Track.
highlights: Sandy beach on the Murrumbidgee River
Large destination playground for all ages and abilities
Sheltered barbecue and picnic areas
Kayak and canoe launching point
On the Wiradjuri Walking Track

name: Oasis Aquatic Centre
description: The Oasis Aquatic Centre in the middle of Wagga runs year round. Indoors there is a 25-metre pool, leisure pools including the Turbo Pool and mushrooms, toddler pools and a program pool used for swimming lessons and hydrotherapy. Outdoors there is a 50-metre pool and a diving pool with one-metre and three-metre springboards and a five-metre platform. The centre has free barbecues, a children's playground and accessible change rooms, and is used by water polo, diving and triathlon groups.
highlights: Indoor 25 m pool and outdoor 50 m pool
Diving pool with springboards and a 5 m platform
Turbo Pool, mushrooms and toddler pools
Learn to Swim classes for adults and children
Free barbecues and a children's playground

name: Wiradjuri Trail
description: The Wiradjuri Trail is a walking and cycling route of about 42 kilometres that circles much of Wagga Wagga, taking in riverbanks and hilltops. It winds through the Birramal Conservation Area, Silvalite Reserve and Pomingalarna Reserve. The Wollundry Loop, a 12.1 kilometre section, follows part of the Murrumbidgee River and the perimeter of the Wollundry Lagoon, and a popular return route starts at the Visitor Information Centre and takes in Wagga Beach, the Cadell Place laneway murals, Wiradjuri Reserve and Marrambidya Wetland.
highlights: About 42 km of walking and cycling trail
12.1 km Wollundry Loop section
Passes Birramal, Silvalite and Pomingalarna reserves
Links Wagga Beach, Cadell Place murals and Marrambidya Wetland

name: Marrambidya Wetland
description: Marrambidya Wetland is a 20-hectare reserve beside the Murrumbidgee River a few minutes from the city centre. It has two kilometres of connected Grade 2 walking tracks, bird hides for watching waterbirds and an elevated viewing platform over the whole wetland. There is a cultural demonstration area with a Wiradjuri campsite, gunyahs and a bora ring, a Wiradjuri Healing Place, and an outdoor art gallery of works at the car park entry. Dogs on leads are welcome.
highlights: Two kilometres of Grade 2 walking tracks
Bird hides and an elevated viewing platform
Wiradjuri cultural demonstration area and Healing Place
Outdoor art gallery at the entry
Dogs welcome on leads

name: Pomingalarna Reserve
description: Pomingalarna Reserve sits on part of the Wiradjuri Trail about ten minutes from the Wagga Wagga CBD and is used by bushwalkers, runners and riders. A marked 13-kilometre bushland mountain bike trail runs through native bushland where kangaroos, wallabies, lizards and birds are common. The reserve is also home to Wagga Wagga's Multisport Cycling Complex, with a criterium track, BMX track, jump tracks, pump tracks, a cycling education area, a velodrome and a mountain bike playground loop. The climb to the top gives some of the best views back over the city.
highlights: 13 km marked bushland mountain bike trail
Multisport Cycling Complex with criterium and BMX tracks
Velodrome, pump tracks and jump tracks
Cycling education area and mountain bike playground loop
Lookout over Wagga Wagga from the summit

name: Birramal Conservation Area
description: Birramal Conservation Area is a 128-hectare site set aside for environmental conservation, taking in the section of the Wiradjuri Trail between the Olympic Highway and Holbrook Road. It can be explored on foot or by bike and offers views over Wagga Wagga and surrounds. The site protects an endangered White Box Woodland community that supports the locally endangered squirrel glider, and glider poles, new tree plantings and artificial nest boxes are visible along the way.
highlights: 128-hectare conservation area on the Wiradjuri Trail
Endangered White Box Woodland
Squirrel glider habitat with glider poles and nest boxes
Walking and mountain biking with views over the city

name: Victory Memorial Gardens
description: The Victory Memorial Gardens were established in 1925 as a tribute to those who fought and died in the First World War, and were designed by Thomas Kerr, designer of the Sydney Botanic Gardens. They run along the banks of the Wollundry Lagoon in the heart of Wagga Wagga. Visitors commonly feed the ducks and water birds, and the geese cross Ivan Jack Drive with right of way. The land was formerly the site of the Old Police Barracks and its police paddocks.
highlights: Established 1925 as a First World War memorial
Designed by Thomas Kerr
On the banks of Wollundry Lagoon in the CBD
Ducks, geese and water birds
Public toilets and picnic area

name: Forum 6 Cinemas Wagga Wagga
description: Forum 6 is a six-cinema complex in the heart of Wagga Wagga. The programme runs from big blockbusters through to art house features, and also includes classic silver screen movies, operas from the MET, special events and midnight premieres. Session times, trading hours and pricing are published on the cinema's website and Facebook page.
highlights: Six screens in the Wagga CBD
Blockbusters, art house and classic films
MET opera screenings and special events
Wheelchair accessible with vision and hearing support

name: Wagga Bowl
description: Wagga Bowl is a ten pin bowling and entertainment centre on Trail Street, trading seven days. It runs birthday and party packages, sells gift vouchers and has a large media screen over the lanes. A movie and bowl deal runs during the school holidays. Bookings are recommended on Saturdays, Sundays and during school and public holidays.
highlights: Ten pin bowling seven days a week
Birthday and party packages
Gift vouchers available
Movie and bowl deal in school holidays
Bookings recommended on weekends and holidays

name: Vortex Entertainment
description: Vortex Entertainment is an indoor entertainment centre in the Wagga CBD. Attractions include six-metre rock climbing walls, a high ropes course, a ninja course, dedicated toddler play areas, bumper cars, virtual reality experiences and 18 holes of mini golf. It also has private party rooms and a cafe serving hot and cold food and drinks, and runs quiet sessions.
highlights: Six-metre rock climbing walls
High ropes and ninja courses
18 holes of indoor mini golf
Bumper cars and virtual reality
Toddler play areas and private party rooms

name: Noah's Ark Indoor Play Centre
description: Noah's Ark is an indoor play and party centre on Hammond Avenue for children under 12, air-conditioned year round. Equipment includes slides, ball pools, flying foxes, crawl tunnels, squeeze rollers and a cosy coupe car track, and plaster painting is also available. The cafe serves hot and cold food along with kids' meals. Socks are required.
highlights: Play and party centre for children under 12
Slides, ball pools, flying foxes and crawl tunnels
Cosy coupe car track and plaster painting
Cafe with kids' meals
Air-conditioned year round

name: Wagga Wagga Sailing Club
description: The Wagga Wagga Sailing Club races on Lake Albert and has around 40 members, with twenty to twenty-five sailors racing regularly. Racing is each Saturday through the season, with briefing at 2pm and the start at 2.30pm. Visitors are welcome to bring their own boat or use a club boat, and crew positions are available. The club runs learn to sail courses through the warmer months and has a radio-controlled sailing section.
highlights: Saturday racing on Lake Albert, briefing 2pm
Around 40 members
Club boats available for visitors
Learn to sail courses in the warmer months
Radio-controlled yacht sailing section

name: Wagga City Aero Club
addressLine: General Aviation Precinct, Elizabeth Avenue, Wagga Wagga Airport
description: The Wagga City Aero Club has its clubhouse in the General Aviation Precinct on Elizabeth Avenue at Wagga Wagga Airport. Members include pilots of all ages and experience, aircraft owners and non-pilots, drawn from general aviation, airlines, commercial and recreational flying and the military. Social evenings run every Friday from 5.30pm, and a barbecue with flying competitions is held on the first Sunday of each month from noon. The club also runs a Young Eagles program for young people.
highlights: Clubhouse at Wagga Wagga Airport's general aviation precinct
Social evenings every Friday from 5.30pm
Barbecue and flying competitions first Sunday of the month
Young Eagles program for young people
New members and non-pilots welcome

name: Men's Shed Wagga Wagga
addressLine: Best Reserve, corner of Veale Street and Ashmont Avenue
description: Men's Shed Wagga Wagga Inc operates from Best Reserve on the corner of Veale Street and Ashmont Avenue. The shed runs a garage sale from Monday to Thursday between 8.15am and 11.45am, with items for sale changing regularly. The phone is answered between 8am and noon on weekdays.
highlights: Based at Best Reserve, Veale Street and Ashmont Avenue
Garage sale Monday to Thursday, 8.15am to 11.45am
Stock for sale changes regularly
Phone answered 8am to noon weekdays

name: Wagga Wagga & District Family History Society
description: The Wagga Wagga & District Family History Society runs a library and research rooms at 24 Tarakan Avenue, Ashmont, open to the public and staffed by volunteers. Its collections include the Pastoral Review journals from 1891 to 1977, which contain photographs of First World War servicemen and nurses contributed by families. The society publishes research CDs, including a Wagga Wagga and district births, deaths, marriages and in memoriams index with more than 49,500 entries.
highlights: Public research rooms and library at Ashmont
Pastoral Review journal collection 1891-1977
Wagga Wagga and district BDM index on CD
Volunteer staffed, phone ahead to confirm opening
Extended hours to 4pm Mondays and Wednesdays during daylight saving

name: Wagga Wagga & District Historical Society
description: The Wagga Wagga & District Historical Society researches and publishes local history and takes enquiries through its website and Facebook page. It does not keep a public room; its historical material is held by Charles Sturt University Regional Archives, the Museum of the Riverina and the Wagga Wagga City Library local history collection. The society was one of the local partners that funded the digitisation of the Wagga Wagga Rate and Valuation books now available through NSW State Archives, and it publishes the Bidgee Whaler articles written by Sylvia Walsh.
highlights: Local history research and publishing
Collections held at CSU Regional Archives, Museum of the Riverina and the city library
Partner in digitising the Wagga Wagga Rate and Valuation books
Bidgee Whaler article archive online
Enquiries by email and through the website

name: Wagga Cycling Club
description: Wagga Cycling Club is a family orientated club focused on track, criterium and road racing. Its coaches run rider development programs for all ages at training nights across the summer and winter seasons. The club holds road racing events in winter and the Golden Wheel two day track carnival in summer.
highlights: Track, criterium and road disciplines
Coached rider development programs for all ages
Training nights in summer and winter seasons
Winter road racing program
Golden Wheel two day track carnival in summer

name: Wagga Wagga Combined Hockey Association
description: Wagga Hockey runs the local hockey competitions at the Jubilee Park Hockey Complex on artificial playing surfaces. Junior competitions are mixed and start at Under 9, Under 11, Under 13 and Under 16, all played on Friday nights. There are three divisions each of men's and women's competition, with senior matches on Saturday afternoons from 11am and lights on both fields allowing play into the evening. The association was formed after the 2005 season when the separate men's and women's associations merged.
highlights: Games at the Jubilee Park Hockey Complex
Mixed junior competitions from Under 9 to Under 16 on Friday nights
Three divisions each of men's and women's competition
Senior matches Saturday afternoons from 11am
Formed in 2005 from the men's and women's associations

name: Football Wagga
description: Football Wagga is the association that runs organised football in Wagga Wagga, covering MiniRoos, junior and senior competitions along with a Football4All AllStars competition and a skill acquisition development program. It publishes fixtures and results, manages referees and coordinates ground availability and closures, with Rawlings Park as the main venue.
highlights: MiniRoos, junior and senior competitions
Football4All AllStars inclusive competition
Skill acquisition and development programs
Referee appointments and development
Fixtures, results and ground closures published online

name: Wagga Wagga Bridge Club
description: The Wagga Wagga Bridge Club plays at 7 Bolton Street and runs sessions each week spread between daytime and evening time slots. It offers free beginner classes and welcomes visitors and new members. The club is affiliated with the Australian Bridge Federation and awards ABF masterpoints, and it hosts congresses that draw players from other clubs.
highlights: Clubrooms at 7 Bolton Street
Weekly daytime and evening sessions
Free beginner classes
Affiliated with the Australian Bridge Federation
Hosts the annual Wagga Wagga Congress

name: Wagga City Golf Club
description: Wagga City Golf Club is about five minutes west of the Wagga Wagga CBD off the Sturt Highway at 5 McNickle Road, Moorong. The course is open every day except Christmas Day from 6am to 6pm, and there is no requirement to be a member to play, with social golfers welcome. The club has a pro shop, offers lessons and vouchers, and hosts corporate golf days and functions. Light refreshments including sandwiches, pies and sausages are available, along with soft drinks and mid strength beers. There is no driving range.
highlights: Open every day except Christmas Day, 6am to 6pm
Social golfers welcome without membership
Pro shop and golf lessons
Corporate golf days and functions
Five minutes west of the CBD off the Sturt Highway

name: Wagga Wagga Country Club
description: The Wagga Wagga Country Club sits on the shores of Lake Albert and is included in Australia's top 100 country courses. The tree-lined 18-hole championship course measures 6054 metres from the back markers and has bent greens and all-weather fairways. The club also caters for functions and dining and has a bar and conference facilities.
highlights: 18-hole championship course of 6054 metres from the back markers
Bent greens and all-weather fairways
On the shores of Lake Albert
Bar, dining and function facilities
Listed among Australia's top 100 country courses

name: Wagga Wagga School of Arts Community Theatre
description: SoACT, the Wagga Wagga School of Arts Community Theatre, is a community theatre company that stages a season of plays and musicals each year and posts audition notices for each production. Recent seasons have included The Sound of Music, The Pirates of Penzance, And Then There Were None, A Broadcast Coup and The Female of the Species, along with the Riverina Water Ten x 10 Playfest of short plays. The company sells memberships and show gift vouchers.
highlights: Community theatre company staging a full season each year
Riverina Water Ten x 10 Playfest of short plays
Open audition notices for each production
Memberships and show gift vouchers
Archive of past production videos for members

name: Wagga Wagga Swim Club
description: Established in 1897, the Wagga Wagga Swim Club is one of the oldest swimming clubs in New South Wales. It runs five squads from Development through to National, plus a Masters and recreational squad, and is led by head coach Gennadiy Labara with a committee and technical officials. The club holds club nights and club championships, enters carnivals and representative meets, and welcomes visiting swimmers.
highlights: Established in 1897
Five squads from Development to National level
Masters and recreational squad
Club nights and club championships
Visiting swimmers welcome

name: Murrumbidgee Landcare
description: Murrumbidgee Landcare Inc is a natural resource management organisation with its office in the Tulloch Business Offices at 66 Coleman Street, Turvey Park. Its staff include a chief executive officer, a manager of projects and partnerships, a regional Landcare coordinator and a regional Aboriginal Landcare coordinator, working from the Wagga Wagga office through the week. It runs projects, events and resources for Landcare groups across the Murrumbidgee.
highlights: Wagga Wagga office in the Tulloch Business Offices
Regional Landcare coordination across the Murrumbidgee
Regional Aboriginal Landcare coordinator
Projects, events and resources for member groups

name: ErinEarth
description: ErinEarth is a sustainable living education centre and volunteering community on Kildare Street in Turvey Park. The garden demonstrates organic vegetable growing and a water-efficient native plant garden, and is set up as a quiet space for nature connection, reflection and nature play. It hosts regular community open days, education sessions and a weekly garden volunteering program on Thursday mornings.
highlights: Organic vegetable growing demonstration garden
Water-efficient native plant garden
Weekly volunteering program on Thursday mornings
Regular community open days
Education and community engagement programs

name: Wagga Basketball
description: Wagga Basketball, home of the Heat, runs junior and senior competitions for around 1000 members at PCYC Wagga Wagga. It fields representative teams in junior and senior leagues from Under 12s through to open divisions in the Waratah State League and other competitions. Programs include Aussie Hoops, an academy program and Blazing Hoops, a free girls program, and the association is run by a volunteer board.
highlights: Junior and senior competitions at PCYC Wagga Wagga
Around 1000 members
Representative teams from Under 12s to open age
Waratah State League representation
Aussie Hoops, academy and free Blazing Hoops girls programs

name: Temora Aviation Museum
description: The Temora Aviation Museum is built on the site of the former No. 10 Elementary Flying Training School, established by the RAAF in May 1941, and holds a flying collection of Australian ex-military aircraft. Visitors can take a guided tour with a volunteer or explore at their own pace with audio-visual presentations, watch a film in the 38-seat surround sound theatre, and see engineers at work from the viewing platform. There are landscaped gardens, picnic areas, an aviation themed playground, flight simulators and a cafe, and Aircraft Showcase flying days are held through the year.
highlights: Flying collection of Australian ex-military aircraft
Guided tours by volunteers and an audio tour
38-seat surround sound theatre
Aviation themed children's playground
Aircraft Showcase flying days and flight simulators

name: Lake Centenary
description: Lake Centenary is four kilometres north of Temora and is used for power boating, water skiing, sailing, canoeing, swimming and fishing. A path circumnavigates the lake for walkers. The precinct also has a playground, self-weighted gym equipment, landscaped picnic areas and free barbecue facilities.
highlights: Power boating, water skiing and canoeing
Swimming and fishing
Path circling the lake
Playground and outdoor gym equipment
Free barbecues and landscaped picnic areas

name: Junee Licorice & Chocolate Factory
description: The Junee Licorice & Chocolate Factory makes organic licorice and chocolate in a historic Junee flour mill and sells it across Australia and overseas. Visitors can take a guided tour of the factory, eat at The Mill Room Cafe and shop the retail range, and the site runs an events program through the year. It opens seven days a week from 9am to 4pm, every day except Anzac Day.
highlights: Organic licorice and chocolate made on site
Guided factory tours
The Mill Room Cafe
Housed in a historic Junee flour mill
Open seven days, 9am to 4pm, except Anzac Day

name: Junee Roundhouse Railway Museum
description: The Junee Roundhouse is one of the few surviving working railway roundhouses in the Southern Hemisphere, unique in Australia for its size, fully circular form and 100 foot turntable. Opened in 1947 as the last steam locomotive depot built for New South Wales Railways, half the building is now a museum while the other half still services locomotives. Exhibits include steam and diesel locomotives, passenger carriages, a sleeping car, a rail motor, a mail van, the only workable steam driven accident crane in New South Wales and a large working model railway. Guided tour information is available at the admissions desk and self-guided tours are welcome.
highlights: Working railway roundhouse with a 100 foot turntable
Steam and diesel locomotives and heritage carriages
The only workable steam driven accident crane in NSW
Large working model railway
Guided and self-guided tours, last admission 3.30pm

name: Junee Golf Club
description: Junee Golf Club plays an 18 hole, par 72 course. There are no bunkers but a couple of holes have out of bounds and other hazards, so club selection and accuracy matter. The course suits both average and longer hitters and is used for social rounds and competition. The clubhouse is managed by volunteers, has a bar and barbecue, and the club hosts regular events and private functions. Campsites are available at the grounds.
highlights: 18 hole, par 72 course
No bunkers but several out of bounds holes
Volunteer managed clubhouse with a bar
Barbecue and camping sites on site
Available for private functions

name: Dog on the Tuckerbox
description: The Dog on the Tuckerbox pioneer monument stands five miles, or eight kilometres, north of Gundagai just off the Hume Highway. The statue was unveiled on 28 November 1932, honouring the bullock drivers who opened up the country and the dogs that travelled with them, a legend carried further by Jack O'Hagan's song. The precinct today has maintained gardens, Australian animal figurines, picnic areas and parking for cars, caravans and coaches, plus a kiosk and farm shop selling food, coffee, local produce and gifts. The Dog's Birthday is celebrated each November.
highlights: Pioneer monument unveiled 28 November 1932
Eight kilometres north of Gundagai off the Hume Highway
Kiosk and farm shop open seven days
Gardens, animal figurines and picnic areas
Parking for cars, caravans and coaches

name: Lake Talbot Water Park
description: Lake Talbot Water Park at Narrandera has pools and three water slides, including an enclosed high-speed racer slide, plus a splash-and-play park. The lawned pool surrounds have shady picnic spots, barbecues and pool-level change rooms, and there is wheelchair access into the pools. A Skywalk off the car park gives views over Lake Talbot itself.
highlights: Three water slides including an enclosed racer slide
Splash-and-play park
Wheelchair access into the pools
Lawned surrounds with barbecues and picnic spots
Skywalk with views over Lake Talbot

name: Calabria Family Wines Riverina Cellar Door
description: The Calabria Family Wines Riverina cellar door is a Tuscan-style tasting room at Griffith, open seven days. It offers classic and premium wine flights, a 45-minute seated tasting of up to eight wines at the cellar door bar poured in Spiegelau glasses with a light platter, and a Sip and Unwind session. An Italian bar menu with antipasto, arancini and focaccia is served between 11am and 2pm, and the site includes a winery museum and an interactive sensory wall. Bookings are strongly recommended and walk-ins are taken if time permits.
highlights: Tuscan-style cellar door open seven days
Classic, premium and Sip and Unwind tasting experiences
45-minute seated flight of up to eight wines
Italian bar menu served 11am to 2pm
Winery museum and interactive sensory wall
